summary:
Slot rule v2 is a lexical answer-type abstention rule for the extractive generator. It fixes every F6 verdict issue (a) to (f). It is safe: answerable acceptance is 98.4% to 100% on every set, held-out included. But it is close to a no-op on external data: LongMemEval balanced 52.6% (+2.6 over no-abstention), LoCoMo 50.0% (+0.0). It therefore FAILS the default-on adoption rule (+3 balanced on both externals) and can ship only as opt-in, which is how the patch ships it: library default abstain_threshold=None, CLI `ask --abstain`. It is not worse than no-abstention on any set. Unlike F6 (49.1%), it no longer falls below 50% on LoCoMo.

How the rule works. The question first gets a typed slot or none:
- name: only for wh-questions asking for an unknown name.
- entity: city / country / school / company ... used as the question's head noun.
- occupation: only when it asks about a person's job.
- frequency, money, duration, distance.
- No slot for yes/no, why/how, advice, choice ("X or Y"), counting/aggregation ("in total", "times", "so far") or date arithmetic ("ago", "since", "between", "have been"). The quantity slot is gone; "how many" is kept only for "how many <time unit>/<length unit>" or "how many times a week".

The evidence is the best-reranked source plus every source with logit >= 0. Sources spoken by a different named speaker than the one in the question are dropped. Metadata lines (speaker:, session_date:, Summary:) are removed. Name/occupation questions about a relative are anchored to sentences that mention that relation or a name introduced next to it. Numeric slots need the filler within one sentence of a content word from the question. Fillers are:
- Unicode-aware capitalised runs that are new relative to the query and not sentence-initial common words.
- A whole-word occupation lexicon (~200 words) plus phrases like "works as", "retired" or "runs a <business>".
- Typed regexes for money, duration, distance and frequency.

The tau floor defaults to off (0.0). It is still available as an optional threshold in (0, 1) but is not recommended.

About this run. The design was built and FROZEN by an earlier, interrupted run of this same workflow stage, at 2026-10-11T22:00:01Z. In this run I:
- checked that all five frozen sha256 hashes still match;
- reproduced the dev numbers from the saved contexts;
- finished the interrupted LoCoMo context collection with the frozen code (my only heavy job);
- replayed all three held-out sets exactly once;
- ran the full test suite;
- rebuilt and re-verified the patch.

The design was not changed after any held-out number existed. The F6 replay on my external contexts reproduces the verifier's numbers exactly (LME 398/470 + 7/30; LoCoMo 1495/1540 + 5/446). That confirms the collection matches theirs.

Root-cause finding for why the externals do not move:
- Benchmark unanswerables ask for an attribute that is simply never stated, so a missing typed filler is a usable signal.
- LongMemEval _abs and LoCoMo category-5 questions are mostly false-premise or entity-swap questions ("What is the name of Maria's one-year-old child?" when the child is John's). The evidence does contain a filler of the right type, just about a different person or event, so a lexical type check cannot fire.
- On LoCoMo, abstention precision is 22.6%, equal to the 22.5% base rate of unanswerables: no signal.
- On LongMemEval it is 22.2% against a 6% base rate: weak signal, but only 2/30 refused.

proposed_changes.description: Adds the slot rule v2: question_slot(query), _slot_evidence(context), _filled_by(...), abstention_reason(context, threshold=ABSTAIN_THRESHOLD, *, slot_check=True) (pure function of context, returns a reason string or None), and answer(..., abstain_threshold=None). The rule is off when abstain_threshold is None (the default). ABSTAIN_THRESHOLD=0.0 means slot rule only, no logit floor. The rule is a no-op unless context['reranker']['status']=='applied' and at least one source has a numeric context['scores'][id]['reranker']. The extractive abstain payload is {'answer':'Insufficient memory evidence.','abstain':True,'reason':'unfilled_<slot>_slot','statements':[],'sources':{}}. The Gemini path is unchanged. Imports only re and math; no new dependencies. The full hunk (+357 lines) is in the patch file, lines 1-372; key hunks shown.

--- a/main/retrieval/generation.py
+++ b/main/retrieval/generation.py
@@ -2,8 +2,10 @@
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import json
+import math
 import os
 from pathlib import Path
+import re
@@ -80,12 +82,357 @@
-def answer(context, *, generator='gemini', client=None, env_file='.env'):
+ABSTAIN_THRESHOLD = 0.0   # slot rule only; a value in (0, 1) adds a sigmoid(max logit) floor (not recommended)
+_META_LINE = re.compile(r'^(?:speaker|session_date|summary):[^\n]*$', re.M | re.I)
+_WORD = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_](?:[\w'’\-]*[^\W_])?")   # Unicode-aware words
+_OCCUPATIONS = """accountant actor ... nurse ... vet veterinarian vicar waiter waitress welder writer""".split()
+_OCCUPATION_EVIDENCE = re.compile(r"\b(?:" + '|'.join(_OCCUPATIONS) + r")(?:e?s)?\b" r"|\b(?:works?|worked|working|job|career|employed|trained|qualified|hired|freelances?|freelancing)\s+(?:as|in)\b" ...)
+_AGGREGATION = re.compile(r"\b(?:in total|total|totally|altogether|all together|combined|so far|overall|sum|different|counting|including|times|each|per)\b")
+_DATE_ARITHMETIC = re.compile(r"\b(?:ago|since|between|passed|elapsed|left|remaining|until|till|after|before|when)\b|\b(?:have|has|had)\b.*\bbeen\b|^(?:long|many\s+[\w-]+|far)\s+(?:have|has|had)\b")
+_SLOT_QUESTIONS = (('name', ...), ('occupation', ...), ('entity', ...), ('frequency', ...), ('money', ...), ('duration', ...), ('distance', ...))
+
+def question_slot(query):
+    """The typed answer slot a question asks for, or None. Yes/no and computed-answer questions have none."""
+    q = _POLITE.sub('', _fold(query).strip())
+    if re.match(_AUX, q):
+        return None
+    for slot, pattern in _SLOT_QUESTIONS:
+        if not pattern.search(q):
+            continue
+        if slot == 'name' and any(word[:1].isupper() for word in re.findall(r"\b(?:called|named)\s+(\S+)", query)):
+            return None   # the name is already given
+        if slot == 'entity' and not _ENTITY_HEAD.search(query):
+            continue
+        rest = q.split('how', 1)[-1].strip() if slot in ('duration', 'distance', 'money') else q
+        if slot in ('duration', 'distance') and (_AGGREGATION.search(rest) or _DATE_ARITHMETIC.search(rest)):
+            return None   # computed
+        if slot == 'money' and _AGGREGATION.search(rest):
+            return None
+        return slot
+    return None
+ ... _speakers, _sentences, _capitalised, _names, _relation_names, _slot_evidence, _filled_by, _filled ...
+    # Evidence: the best-scored source plus every source the cross-encoder judged relevant (logit >= 0),
+    # minus sources spoken by a different named speaker than the one the question is about.
+    keys = [key for key in scored if key == best or scored[key] >= 0]
+ ...
+def abstention_reason(context, threshold=ABSTAIN_THRESHOLD, *, slot_check=True):
+    if threshold is None:
+        return None
+    evidence = _slot_evidence(context)
+    if evidence is None:
+        return None
+    if threshold > 0:
+        ... return 'low_reranker_confidence' if max logit < logit(threshold)
+    slot, sentences, excluded, extra = evidence
+    if not slot_check or slot is None:
+        return None
+    return None if _filled(slot, sentences, excluded, extra) else f"unfilled_{slot.replace('relation_', '')}_slot"
+
+def answer(context, *, generator='gemini', client=None, env_file='.env', abstain_threshold=None):
     if generator not in {'gemini', 'extractive'}:
         raise ValueError('Unknown answer generator')
+    if abstain_threshold is not None and not 0 <= abstain_threshold < 1:
+        raise ValueError('abstain_threshold must be in [0, 1)')
     if not context['sources']:
         return {...}
     if generator == 'extractive':
+        reason = abstention_reason(context, abstain_threshold)
+        if reason:
+            return {'answer': 'Insufficient memory evidence.', 'abstain': True, 'reason': reason,
+                    'statements': [], 'sources': {}, 'generator': generator}
         payload = {'abstain': False, 'reason': '', 'statements': [...]}

dev_results:
Tuning used only dev data. Contexts: hybrid_full, pool 20, exact search. Files: out/ctx_calib.json (author's abstention_dev.json, 45A/45U) and out/ctx_bench_dev.json (benchmark dev split, 83A/7U).

| Rule | Dev-calib accepted | Dev-calib refused | Dev-calib balanced | Bench-dev accepted | Bench-dev refused | Bench-dev balanced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No abstention | 45/45 | 0/45 | 50.0% | 83/83 | 0/7 | 50.0% |
| F6 | 36/45 | 5/45 | 45.6% | 83/83 | 2/7 | 64.3% |
| Template prior | 20/45 | 10/45 | 33.3% | 79/83 | 3/7 | 69.0% |
| v2 | 45/45 | 11/45 | 62.2% | 83/83 | 3/7 | 71.4% |

- **Abstention precision for v2:** 100% on both dev sets.
- **Grounded correctness:** calib (computed rows excluded) 57.3% vs 43.9% for no abstention. Bench-dev 93.3% vs 90.0%.
- **v2's calib refusals:** 5 name, 2 entity, 2 duration, 1 money, 1 occupation.
- **What v2 misses on calib:** 34 of 45. They are mostly attribute types with no slot by design:
  - dates, counts, scores, opinions, why, which-option, yes/no existence, advice;
  - all 6 cross-persona traps, where the evidence does contain a filler of the right type from the other persona's memories.
- **The template prior** now does badly on the author's diversified dev set (33.3% calib). The new unanswerables broke the benchmark-template shortcut.

Design choices backed by dev evidence only (tools/variants.py):
- **Evidence set.** "Best source + logit >= 0" ties "best only" and "logit >= -2 or best" (62.2% / 71.4%). It beats "all context sources" (56.7% / 64.3%) and "top-2" (57.8% / 71.4%). Dropping the speaker filter loses 1 calib refusal. I kept "best + logit >= 0" over "best only" because it is equally good on dev and more tolerant when the best source is a near-duplicate.
- **Tau floor.**
  - A floor at logit -8 or below changes nothing on dev.
  - At -7/-6 it costs 1 bench-dev answerable for +1 calib refusal.
  - At -5 it refuses +1 bench-dev and +2 calib unanswerables but costs 3 bench-dev answerables (96.4% acceptance).
  - At -4/-3 it costs more answerables on both sets.
  - No dev evidence supports a floor, so the default is 0.0 (off).
- **Synthetic phrasing probe** (designer-written, not held-out, partly used during design): 0/40 false abstentions on answerable phrasings, including the verifier's examples ("My brother is a nurse", "Is my dog called Biscuit?", "Did I ever meet someone named Carlos?"). 10/10 refusals on the unanswerable ones.

- **Benchmark test**
  - Official run: `python -m evaluation.ablation --split test --candidate-limit 20 --abstain-threshold 0.0`, hybrid_full (heldout/bench_test_v2/results.json).
  - Result: answerable accepted 99.6% (246/247), unanswerable refused 17.4% (4/23), balanced 58.5%, grounded 90.4%.
  - The replay from heldout/ctx_bench_test.json gives the same numbers.
  - Abstention precision 80% (4/5). The one false abstention is a duration slot.
  - Refusals: 2 money, 2 occupation.
- **LongMemEval oracle** (user turns as memories, 500 questions, _abs = should refuse)
  - Accepted 463/470 (98.5%), 405/411 when gold evidence is in context. Refused 2/30 (6.7%). Balanced 52.6%, +2.6 over no-abstention. Precision 22.2% (2/9). Grounded 31.4%, unchanged.
  - The 7 false abstentions are "How many days did I spend…" style duration questions that need aggregation (4), 1 name, 1 money, 1 entity.
- **LoCoMo** (1986 questions, category 5 = should refuse)
  - Accepted 1516/1540 (98.4%), 972/982 with gold in context. Refused 7/446 (1.6%). Balanced 50.0% (50.006%), +0.0. Precision 22.6% (7/31), equal to the 22.5% unanswerable base rate. Grounded 16.7% vs 16.5%.
  - False abstentions: 8 duration, 7 entity, 5 name, 3 frequency, 1 occupation.

**Adoption rule verdict: FAIL for default-on, so opt-in only.**
- The acceptance thresholds pass on all three sets (99.6% >= 95%; 98.5% and 98.4% >= 90%).
- The balanced gain is +2.6 on LongMemEval and +0.0 on LoCoMo, under the required +3 on both.
- The design is NOT worse than no-abstention on any external set (LoCoMo ties to within 0.01 points). F6 was worse on LoCoMo (49.1%).

**Baselines on held-out**
- **F6** reproduces the verifier exactly: LME 84.7% / 23.3% / 54.0%, LoCoMo 97.1% / 1.1% / 49.1%. On the new bench test it gets 98.8% / 13.0% / 55.9%.
- **Template prior:** bench test 95.1% / 17.4% / 56.3%, LME 51.1% / 73.3% / 62.2%, LoCoMo 93.5% / 5.2% / 49.3%. Its LME balanced score is higher, but it rejects half of all answerables (212 quantity questions), so it is unusable.

risks:
1. **External signal is small to none.** LoCoMo precision equals the base rate. A lexical type check cannot detect false-premise or entity-swap unanswerables, where a filler of the right type exists but belongs to another person or event. This is the dominant unanswerable kind in LongMemEval _abs, LoCoMo category 5 and the author's cross-persona traps (v2 refused 0/6 traps). Recommend shipping opt-in only (as patched), or not at all. A real gain needs an entity/premise-aware answerability model (the parallel "answerability-model" design) or leaving abstention to the LLM generator.
2. **Benchmark-specific tuning risk.** The lexicons and patterns were developed against the dev calibration set and a designer-written probe. Bench-dev has only 7 unanswerables, so dev balanced figures are noisy: one question moves bench-dev balanced by 7 points.
3. **Remaining false abstentions** (about 1.5% of answerables on externals):
   - "How many days did I spend…" questions that need summing across memories;
   - entity questions where the place is stated only through context ("in Chicago" written earlier);
   - name questions whose answer is lowercase or written in quotes.
4. **Brittle by nature.** Hand-written English-only patterns; non-English questions mostly get no slot, which means no abstention. That is safe, but it means no coverage.
5. **Process note.** The design was authored and frozen by an earlier, interrupted run of this stage. This run verified the freeze hashes, reproduced the dev numbers and completed only the held-out evaluation, without modifying the rule. Held-out benchmark-test numbers use the author's new unanswerables and are not comparable with F6's earlier 86.3%.
6. **Labels.** The dev calibration and benchmark labels are AI-authored and not human-validated. False-premise unanswerables could also be "answered" with "no record", and text-matching scorers may treat that differently.
7. **Aliases.** The yes/no aliases in abstention_dev.json are loose ('yes', '2'). They affect only grounded correctness on calib, not the answerability numbers.
confidence: High that the numbers are correct and reproducible: the F6 external replay matches the verifier exactly, and the ablation-harness and replay bench-test numbers agree. High that the design fails the default-on adoption rule (+2.6 / +0.0 against the required +3 / +3). Medium that it generalises safely as opt-in: acceptance is at least 98.4% on all held-out sets, but its refusal power outside the benchmark is near zero.
root_cause: F6 failed for three reasons. First, its question patterns matched the benchmark's two unanswerable templates, so it worked as a prior over wording. Second, its slots fired on computed questions (counting, date arithmetic), on yes/no questions and on questions that already contained the name. Third, its evidence detectors were buggy: dead occupation alternatives, ASCII-only capitalisation, and the Summary: line counted as a name. v2 removes all of these, and its false abstentions drop to about 1.5% of answerables. The remaining limit is structural. External unanswerables are mostly false-premise or entity-swap questions where a filler of the right type exists in the evidence. A rule that only checks whether a filler of the asked-for type is present therefore cannot separate them from answerable questions.
